User: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves nondisclosure agreement dispute. My lawyer is Lisa Park with Park Legal Group; we have proceedings at the federal district court. We're past the filing stage and waiting for the court calendar.. Opposing party: my former landlord. This is in King County, Washington. The contract was signed last year and they've since stopped performing. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about what documents I should bring and what to say in the hearing? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.
Assistant: I can help you get organized and ready to consult with Lisa Park and to participate if needed at the hearing. Below is a practical, attorney-focused checklist you can bring to your meeting plus short scripts and points to rehearse. This is general guidance — confirm strategy and specifics with Lisa.

1) Top questions to ask your attorney (Lisa Park)
- What is the specific purpose of the upcoming hearing (status/scheduling conference, motion hearing, temporary relief, etc.)?
- What relief are we seeking from the court at this hearing (e.g., injunctive relief, enforcement, damages, discovery timetable)?
- Which documents and exhibits do you want me to bring and in what format (originals, certified copies, hard copies for the judge/court reporter/opposing counsel, electronic copies)?
- Do you want me to prepare a signed declaration/affidavit? If so, what facts should it include and how should it be formatted?
- Will I need to testify at the hearing? If yes, what will I be asked and how should I prepare?
- Are there threshold legal issues (jurisdiction, enforceability of the NDA, statute of frauds, waiver, mitigation) we should be prepared to address?
- What arguments do you expect the opposing party (former landlord) to raise, and what are our responses?
- Is there a protective order or sealing request needed because the dispute involves an NDA?
- Are there outstanding discovery needs we should push for before the hearing? Any motions you recommend (e.g., motion to compel, motion for preliminary injunction, fees)?
- What are the likely next steps and timeline after this hearing?
- Are there settlement considerations I should be ready to discuss? Who will handle settlement talks — you or me?

2) Document checklist to gather and organize
Organize everything chronologically in a binder (tabbed) and also collect electronic copies (PDFs). Label exhibits clearly.

Essential contract and core records
- The signed nondisclosure agreement (NDA) — fully executed copy, any amendments
- The lease (if relevant) and any related contracts between you and the landlord
- Any written notices regarding the landlord’s performance or nonperformance (letters, emails)
- Dates: when the NDA was signed, when performance stopped, any notices/demands to cure

Communications and contemporaneous records
- All emails, texts, letters, messages between you and the landlord relevant to the NDA or dispute
- Communications with any third parties referencing the NDA or alleged disclosures
- Notes from phone calls or meetings (dates, attendees, summary)

Performance / nonperformance and damages
- Proof you performed your obligations (if applicable): invoices, receipts, work logs
- Evidence of landlord’s failure to perform: withheld services, stopped payments, breach notices
- Financial records showing damages: invoices, bank statements, lost business evidence, receipts
- Mitigation steps you took (what you did to reduce damages)

Prior demands / efforts to resolve
- Copies of demand letters, requests to cure, settlement offers, and responses
- Any correspondence with your attorney about settlement

Court filings and litigation documents (bring originals/copies)
- Complaint, answer, counterclaims, motions already filed
- Any prior affidavits/declarations or exhibits filed with the court
- Court notices, scheduling orders, and local rules you were provided

Witnesses & declarations
- Contact info and summaries for potential witnesses (names, roles, what they saw)
- Draft or signed declarations from witnesses (if already prepared)
- Your personal declaration: timeline and factual statements you can sign

Evidence authenticity & chain of custody
- Metadata for emails or electronic files if possible (dates/timestamps)
- Any copies vs. originals notes (where originals are stored)

Confidentiality & privileged material
- Mark which documents are attorney-client or privileged; discuss with Lisa about what can be shared and whether to seek protective order or sealing.

3) What to say at the hearing — concise structure and scripts
Work with Lisa on the legal script; below are short, neutral templates you can adapt and rehearse:

If you are asked to give a brief statement or answer questions
- Very short opening: “Good morning, Your Honor. My name is [Your Name]. I’m a party in this case. I’m here to support counsel and provide facts about the nondisclosure agreement and how the other party stopped performing as of [date].”
- Key facts to convey (one-sentence bullets): when the NDA was signed; what obligation the landlord failed to perform; when you discovered the nonperformance; what harm you’ve suffered; what relief you seek.
- If questioned, answer briefly, stick to facts, give dates, and avoid legal conclusions — leave legal argument to Lisa.

If Lisa asks you to testify or read a declaration
- Prepare a chronological narrative but keep each answer factual and concise.
- Refer to specific exhibits (e.g., “As shown in Exhibit 3, email dated MM/DD/YYYY…”).
- If you don’t remember a detail precisely, say so and offer to check records rather than guessing.

If Lisa wants you to present a short summary to the court (2–3 minutes)
- Opening line: state the issue and relief succinctly.
  Example: “Your Honor, this is an NDA enforcement matter. The parties signed the agreement on [date]. The landlord stopped performing the confidentiality obligations on [date], causing [specific harm]. We ask the Court to [specific relief].”
- Key evidence: name 2–3 strongest pieces (the signed NDA, a post-breach email, and a damage exhibit).
- Close: “We are prepared to proceed with discovery as directed and ask the court to set [specific next step].”

4) Anticipate opposing arguments and how to respond (talk with Lisa about these)
- Opposing will likely argue: NDA unenforceable, lack of specificity, no breach, mitigation failure, lack of damages, or that the alleged disclosures were permitted. Have factual counters ready:
  - Point to the exact NDA provisions and the landlord’s communications that show nonperformance.
  - Show contemporaneous evidence (email/text) that contradicts their claims.
  - Show damages and mitigation steps.

5) Logistics for the hearing and exhibits
- Bring at least: 3–5 paper copies of each exhibit (judge, court clerk, opposing counsel) unless instructed otherwise; also bring a complete exhibit binder for yourself and one electronic set on a USB if allowed.
- Number exhibits consistently (Exhibit 1, 2, …). Make a short exhibit list.
- Arrive 30–60 minutes early; bring photo ID, case number, counsel contact info.
- Wear professional attire and be prepared for security screening.

6) Preparation & rehearsal
- Meet with Lisa to review your declaration and exhibits line-by-line.
- Role-play likely questions with Lisa so you can answer crisply.
- Ask Lisa to give you exact statements you should avoid (e.g., do not volunteer settlement negotiations, do not admit anything that might be privileged).

7) Possible legal next steps (so you can discuss strategy)
- Motion schedule (motions to compel, motions for preliminary injunction, summary judgment timeline)
- Discovery deadlines and document requests/subpoenas
- Requests for preservation of evidence
- Protective order or sealing motions if NDA material is at issue
- Settlement negotiation or mediation options

8) Action items for you right now
- Print and organize the document list above; collect the NDA and communications first.
- Draft a clear chronological timeline (dates, short one-line description for each key event).
- Note witness names and contact info and collect brief witness statements.
- Ask Lisa whether she wants a signed declaration and, if so, send her a draft timeline and facts.
- Schedule a prep call with Lisa at least a few days before the hearing.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a compact, editable checklist you can print and bring to your meeting with Lisa.
- Draft a short one-page timeline you can sign as a declaration template for Lisa to review.
- Draft a 2–3 minute hearing script based on the facts you give me.

Would you like any of those templates (checklist, declaration draft, or hearing script)? If yes, tell me which and provide a few key dates and the brief factual timeline (when NDA signed, roughly when they stopped performing, any demand letters, and the type of relief you want).
